title: Lumen
tagline: An infinite canvas that reads what you sketched and offers the next move beside it.
stateNote: A hosted copy runs on my Vercel. It works without an API key, and Claude can be added for generation.
problem: Whiteboards leave the structuring to you, and chat sidebars pull attention away from the canvas. Lumen puts a small set of suggestions right at the thing you selected, so rough notes can become structure and structure can become something that runs.
audience: People who think by sketching, and anyone curious about AI that works on the canvas itself instead of in a chat window.
contribution: Lumen is my project, built on top of Excalidraw's open-source React component. The drawing editor underneath is Excalidraw's work.
worksToday: Select notes, an outline or a flowchart and a dock offers actions that fit that selection, such as clustering, structuring or tidying.
An offline engine handles outlines, arrows, clustering and graph checks with no API key.
Results land on the canvas as ordinary editable objects with undo and version history.
Boards share by link without a server, and everything is stored locally first.
limitations: The feature list comes from the project README. Not every feature has had an independent test pass.
Real-time collaboration across devices needs a small relay you run yourself.
